provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: In the original orientation the grid has a black legend region on top, holding one coloured cell in column 0 on each of rows 1, 3 and 5. Below it is a full divider line of the field background colour, then the field of boxes. The factory transforms two direction vectors with the D4 index. The first is u, the direction from the divider toward the black legend region (originally up). The second is b, the direction in which bars grow (originally right). A horizontal flip negates the column component, and each clockwise rotation maps (dr, dc) to (dc, -dr). The black colour becomes the constant palette[0]. The emitted program works directly in visible coordinates. (1) It scans rows, or columns when u is horizontal, starting from the black side. The first uniform line whose colour is not black is the divider, and its colour is the field background. Scanning from the black side matters because the far edge line of the field is also uniform. (2) The black side of the divider is the legend region. Its non-black cells are the legend cells, and their colours form the key set. (3) On the field side, every colour other than the background and the key colours is erased to the background. (4) For each key colour the program counts 4-connected components in the field. (5) Each legend line, which runs along b and lies entirely in the black region, is cleared to black. It is then painted with min(n, line length) cells of the legend colour, starting at the grid edge opposite b. A count of 0 leaves only black.
draft_notes.limitations: The program assumes the constructor's domain. The black colour (palette[0]) is never the field background or a legend colour. The generator's non-overlap check keeps boxes separated by at least one cell, so the number of 4-connected components of a colour equals the number of boxes of that colour (generator: bcolors.count). This depends on common.overlaps enforcing a 1-cell margin, which I could not check because the common module was not supplied. The optional single-pixel hole in a 2x2 box leaves an L-tromino, which is still one component, so it causes no discrepancy. If no divider line is found, the input is returned unchanged. The demonstrations are not used, because the roles come from the D4 and palette constants plus the visible structure. I found no fixture contradictions or constructor defects. As instructed, no tests were run.

independent_source_review.mechanism: A black legend region holds three distinct colours, one in column 0 of each of rows 1, 3 and 5. A uniform divider row (row 7) follows in the field background colour, then a field of separated rectangular boxes. The output erases every field object whose colour is not in the legend. Each legend cell becomes a bar from the legend edge whose length equals the number of 4-connected components of that colour in the field. The constructor's label is bcolors.count(color). The emitted solver works in visible augmented coordinates using D4-transformed direction constants. u points from the divider toward the black side and b is the bar growth direction. The solver finds the divider by scanning from the black side for the first uniform non-black line. It reads the legend, erases non-key field colours, counts components, clears each legend line and repaints the bar.
evidence: Constructor: subset = random_colors(5|6) draws from 1..9, bgcolor = subset.pop(), colors = sample(subset, 3), bcolors = choices(subset, n). The legend colours are therefore distinct, never black and never the field background. Field box colours are never the background, so erasing a box can never merge it into the divider or background incorrectly.

common.overlaps(..., spacing=1) skips a pair only when a full one-cell gap exists in rows or in columns. Edge-adjacent and diagonally touching boxes are rejected. So 4-connected components of a colour correspond exactly to boxes of that colour, and the label bcolors.count(color) equals the solver's component count. This settles the prior note's unverified assumption.
The optional single-pixel hole is applied only to a 2x2 box and is written to both grid and output. It leaves a connected L-tromino, so the count is unchanged and the erasure stays consistent.

Box geometry: brows in [1, 12-tall] and bcols in [1, 9-wide] keep boxes inside field rows 8..18 and columns 1..8. They never touch the divider row 7 or the grid edges. num_boxes <= 8 < 10, so a bar never exceeds its legend line and min(n, len) never truncates.

Divider scan: black-side lines are either all black (skipped by the line[0] != BLACK test) or contain one legend cell (not uniform). The first uniform non-black line from the black side is therefore the divider. Scanning from the black side avoids the uniform far edge line of the field.

Bar painting clears an entire line through the legend cell along b. Canonically that is row y in {1, 3, 5}, which lies wholly in the black region, and the same holds under every D4 variant. Legend cells sit on distinct lines, so clearing one line never disturbs another legend cell. A count of 0 leaves the line black, matching the constructor's zero-initialised output.

No hidden latent leaks into labels. Everything the label depends on is visible: the legend colours, the box colours and the connectivity. The solver ignores demonstrations, which is legitimate because legend colours are read from the query itself.
The emitted solver uses only the specialised constants BLACK = palette[0], UR/UC and BR/BC in visible coordinates. There is no whole-grid untransform/solve/retransform wrapper.
edcc2ff0 is not in require_colour_evidence's task list (early return). This is appropriate because no arbitrary colour lookup exists; the association is shown by the legend in the query input itself.
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks covering all 8 D4 variants, and 16 fixture variants. The canonical fixtures match the constructor's validate() parameters.
nonblocking_limits: If no divider is found the input is returned unchanged. This is an out-of-domain fallback the constructor never reaches.
The solver assumes palette[0] is the legend-region colour and never a field or legend colour. The constructor guarantees this, since colours come only from 1..9 before palette mapping.
Bars are painted along the whole legend line from the grid edge opposite b. This relies on the legend cell sitting at that edge, which is constructor-guaranteed (column 0 canonically).
The D4 direction convention in build_program was not independently derived against the augmentation module. Its correctness rests on the host audit covering all 8 orientations.

draft_notes.host_review: Per-query legend plus component counts determine bars. Input rectangles are separated; optional2x2hole retains connectivity. D4 direction convention is flip-columns thenclockwise turns as augmentation source confirms; all8execution checks passed.
